name: Sam Altman
blurb: Sam Altman leads OpenAI, the lab behind ChatGPT and the GPT model family that ignited the modern generative-AI era. Under his leadership OpenAI turned frontier research into one of the fastest-adopted consumer and enterprise products in history, reshaping how businesses everywhere think about software.

name: Greg Brockman
blurb: Greg Brockman co-founded OpenAI and, as President, has been the engineering force behind scaling its training infrastructure and shipping products like ChatGPT and the OpenAI API. He previously served as Stripe's first CTO, building the payments platform used across the internet economy.

name: Dario Amodei
blurb: Dario Amodei co-founded Anthropic and leads its development of the Claude model family, pairing frontier capability with pioneering AI-safety research. His work on scaling laws and constitutional AI has shaped how the entire industry trains and aligns large models.

name: Daniela Amodei
blurb: Daniela Amodei co-founded Anthropic and, as President, built its commercial, policy, and operational engine — scaling Claude into one of the most widely deployed enterprise AI assistants. She is a leading voice for responsible scaling policies in frontier AI companies.

name: Jared Kaplan
blurb: Jared Kaplan, a theoretical physicist turned AI researcher, co-authored the seminal scaling-laws papers that predicted how model capability grows with compute — the blueprint for the frontier-model race. As Anthropic's Chief Science Officer he guides the research behind the Claude models.

name: Ilya Sutskever
blurb: Ilya Sutskever co-authored AlexNet, the 2012 result that launched the deep-learning revolution, and as OpenAI's chief scientist drove the research line that produced GPT-4. He now leads Safe Superintelligence Inc., a lab devoted solely to building safe superhuman AI.

name: Mira Murati
blurb: Mira Murati was OpenAI's CTO through the launches of ChatGPT, DALL·E, and GPT-4, translating frontier research into products used by hundreds of millions. In 2025 she founded Thinking Machines Lab, one of the best-funded AI startups ever at inception.

name: Demis Hassabis
blurb: Demis Hassabis co-founded DeepMind and leads Google's unified AI effort, spanning the Gemini models and landmark scientific systems like AlphaGo and AlphaFold. He shared the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for AlphaFold's protein-structure breakthrough, which transformed computational biology.

name: Noam Shazeer
blurb: Noam Shazeer co-authored the 2017 'Attention Is All You Need' paper that introduced the Transformer, the architecture underlying virtually every modern AI model. After founding Character.AI he returned to Google in 2024 to co-lead the Gemini frontier-model effort.

name: Elon Musk
blurb: Elon Musk founded xAI, builder of the Grok models and the Colossus supercomputer — one of the largest AI training clusters ever assembled. Through Tesla's Full Self-Driving and Optimus humanoid programs he is pushing AI into cars, robots, and physical industry at consumer scale.

name: Jensen Huang
blurb: Jensen Huang built NVIDIA from a graphics-chip maker into the multi-trillion-dollar engine of the AI era — its GPUs and CUDA platform train and run nearly every frontier model. His decade-early bet on accelerated computing made him arguably the single most consequential figure in AI infrastructure.

name: Lisa Su
blurb: Lisa Su engineered one of the great turnarounds in tech history at AMD and has positioned its MI-series accelerators as the leading alternative for AI training and inference at scale. Her open-ecosystem strategy is reshaping the economics of AI compute.

name: Satya Nadella
blurb: Satya Nadella made the defining corporate AI bet of the decade — Microsoft's multibillion-dollar OpenAI partnership — and wove Copilot through Windows, Office, and Azure. He turned Microsoft into the distribution engine that brought generative AI to mainstream business.

name: Mustafa Suleyman
blurb: Mustafa Suleyman co-founded DeepMind and Inflection AI before becoming CEO of Microsoft AI, where he leads Copilot and Microsoft's consumer AI products. His book 'The Coming Wave' framed the global debate on governing transformative AI.

name: Kevin Scott
blurb: Kevin Scott, as Microsoft's CTO, architected the company's technical partnership with OpenAI and the Azure supercomputing fleet that trains frontier models. He champions the agentic-web vision and open protocols like MCP for connecting AI systems to real-world software.

name: Sundar Pichai
blurb: Sundar Pichai declared Google an 'AI-first' company back in 2016 and now oversees the Gemini era — frontier models integrated across Search, Android, Cloud, and Workspace for billions of users. Under him Alphabet also commercialized Waymo, the leading US robotaxi service.

name: Jeff Dean
blurb: Jeff Dean built much of Google's foundational infrastructure (MapReduce, Bigtable, TensorFlow) and co-founded Google Brain, the team that incubated the deep-learning boom. As Google's Chief Scientist he guides research strategy behind the Gemini models.

name: Mark Zuckerberg
blurb: Mark Zuckerberg made open-weight AI mainstream by releasing the Llama model family, then launched Meta Superintelligence Labs with one of the most aggressive talent and compute build-outs in the industry. His strategy forced the entire market toward open and personal AI.

name: Yann LeCun
blurb: Yann LeCun pioneered convolutional neural networks, work that earned him the Turing Award and underpins modern computer vision. As Meta's Chief AI Scientist he champions open research and world-model architectures as the path beyond today's LLMs.

name: Alexandr Wang
role: Founder, Scale AI; Chief AI Officer
blurb: Alexandr Wang founded Scale AI at 19 and built it into the data-labeling backbone of the AI industry, serving frontier labs and the US government. Meta's 2025 multibillion-dollar deal brought him in to lead its superintelligence effort — one of the boldest acquihires ever.

name: Nat Friedman
blurb: Nat Friedman, as GitHub CEO, shipped GitHub Copilot — the first mass-market AI coding assistant and proof that LLMs could transform professional work. After backing many top AI startups as an investor, he joined Meta's superintelligence leadership in 2025.

name: Andy Jassy
blurb: Andy Jassy built AWS into the world's largest cloud and now steers Amazon's full-stack AI push: Trainium chips, Bedrock model services, the multibillion-dollar Anthropic partnership, and Alexa's generative reinvention. Amazon under Jassy is the quiet giant of enterprise AI plumbing.

name: Rohit Prasad
blurb: Rohit Prasad led the science behind Alexa, one of the most widely deployed conversational AI systems ever, and now heads Amazon's Artificial General Intelligence team building the Nova frontier models. He oversees one of the largest applied-AI research organizations in industry.

name: Marc Benioff
blurb: Marc Benioff invented the SaaS category with Salesforce and is now betting the company on Agentforce — autonomous AI agents embedded in the world's dominant CRM. He is one of the loudest executive voices arguing that 'digital labor' will redefine enterprise software.

name: Alex Karp
blurb: Alex Karp built Palantir into the leading operational-AI platform for governments and heavy industry, and its AIP product made it one of the best-performing AI stocks of the era. His thesis — that AI value comes from deployment into real institutions, not demos — has been vindicated at scale.

name: Aravind Srinivas
blurb: Aravind Srinivas co-founded Perplexity, the AI answer engine that mounted the first credible challenge to traditional web search in decades. Its cited, conversational answers and Comet browser have made it one of the fastest-growing consumer AI products in the world.

name: Clément Delangue
blurb: Clément Delangue built Hugging Face into the 'GitHub of machine learning' — the default home for over a million open models and datasets. His platform is the connective tissue of open-source AI, used by nearly every company building with machine learning.

name: Ali Ghodsi
blurb: Ali Ghodsi turned Databricks — born from UC Berkeley's Spark project — into one of the most valuable private software companies on earth by fusing data infrastructure with enterprise AI. Its lakehouse platform and MosaicML acquisition made it the place enterprises train and deploy their own models.

name: Matei Zaharia
blurb: Matei Zaharia created Apache Spark, the engine that defined modern big-data processing, and co-founded Databricks where he serves as CTO. His research group also produced MLflow and DSPy, tools that shaped how practitioners build and optimize AI systems.

name: Sridhar Ramaswamy
blurb: Sridhar Ramaswamy ran Google's ads business, founded the AI search engine Neeva, and now leads Snowflake's transformation into an AI data cloud with its Cortex AI services. He is driving one of the fastest enterprise-AI product pivots among large public companies.

name: Bret Taylor
blurb: Bret Taylor — co-creator of Google Maps, former Salesforce co-CEO, and OpenAI's board chair — co-founded Sierra, the benchmark company for AI customer-service agents. Sierra's success has made 'outcome-priced' AI agents a template for the industry.

name: Michael Truell
blurb: Michael Truell co-founded Anysphere, maker of Cursor, the AI-native code editor that became one of the fastest-growing software products ever and redefined how millions of developers write code. Cursor turned 'AI pair programming' from novelty into the daily default.

name: Scott Wu
blurb: Scott Wu, a legendary competitive programmer, co-founded Cognition and launched Devin, the first widely known autonomous AI software engineer. Cognition's acquisition of Windsurf and rapid enterprise adoption put fully agentic coding on every tech roadmap.

name: Amjad Masad
blurb: Amjad Masad built Replit into the platform where anyone can build software with AI agents, making 'vibe coding' accessible to non-programmers worldwide. Replit Agent is one of the clearest demonstrations that natural language is becoming the new programming interface.

name: Harrison Chase
blurb: Harrison Chase created LangChain, the open-source framework that defined how developers compose LLMs into applications, and LangGraph/LangSmith for production agent orchestration. His tools became the de-facto starting point for a generation of AI engineers.

name: Tri Dao
blurb: Tri Dao invented FlashAttention, the algorithm that dramatically accelerated Transformer training and inference and is now baked into virtually every serious AI stack. As Together AI's chief scientist and a Princeton professor, he also co-created the Mamba state-space architecture.

name: Vipul Ved Prakash
blurb: Vipul Ved Prakash co-founded Together AI, the leading independent cloud for open-source models, making frontier-class open models practical for enterprises to fine-tune and serve. His company anchors the open-model economy in the US.

name: Ion Stoica
blurb: Ion Stoica co-founded Databricks and Anyscale and leads Berkeley's Sky Computing Lab, whose projects — Spark, Ray, vLLM — form the infrastructure layer of modern AI. Ray and vLLM alone power training and serving at most major AI companies.

name: May Habib
blurb: May Habib co-founded Writer, the full-stack generative-AI platform whose in-house Palmyra models power content and agentic workflows at hundreds of major enterprises. She proved a startup could compete with frontier labs by focusing narrowly on business work.

name: Daphne Koller
blurb: Daphne Koller, a MacArthur-winning Stanford professor and Coursera co-founder, leads insitro, which uses machine learning to reinvent drug discovery. She is one of the most influential figures applying AI to biology and medicine.

name: Fei-Fei Li
blurb: Fei-Fei Li created ImageNet, the dataset that catalyzed the deep-learning revolution, and co-directs Stanford's Institute for Human-Centered AI. Her startup World Labs is pioneering spatial intelligence — AI that understands and generates 3D worlds.

name: Andrew Ng
blurb: Andrew Ng co-founded Google Brain and Coursera, led Baidu's AI Group, and has taught machine learning to millions through DeepLearning.AI. Through AI Fund he now incubates applied-AI companies, championing the pragmatic, business-first adoption of AI.

name: Andrej Karpathy
blurb: Andrej Karpathy led Tesla's Autopilot vision team and was a founding member of OpenAI; his open courses on building neural networks from scratch educated a generation of AI engineers. He coined 'vibe coding' and now builds Eureka Labs, an AI-native education company.

name: Chelsea Finn
blurb: Chelsea Finn co-founded Physical Intelligence, the multibillion-dollar startup building foundation models for robots, and pioneered meta-learning methods (MAML) at Stanford. Her work is central to giving general-purpose robots the ability to learn any task.

name: Brett Adcock
blurb: Brett Adcock founded Figure, the US humanoid-robot company whose Helix AI and BMW factory deployments made commercial humanoids credible. A serial founder (Archer Aviation, Vettery), he's racing to put general-purpose robots into workplaces and homes.

name: Marc Raibert
role: Founder, Boston Dynamics; ED, The AI Institute
blurb: Marc Raibert founded Boston Dynamics, whose Atlas and Spot robots defined the world's image of advanced robotics for two decades. He now leads the Robotics & AI Institute, pushing the frontier of machines that combine athletic ability with cognitive intelligence.

name: Pieter Abbeel
blurb: Pieter Abbeel pioneered deep reinforcement learning for robotics at Berkeley and co-founded Covariant, whose warehouse-AI team Amazon absorbed in 2024. His students and research underpin much of today's robot-learning industry.

name: David Baker
blurb: David Baker won the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for computational protein design — using AI to create entirely new proteins never seen in nature. His Institute for Protein Design has spun out a wave of companies turning designed proteins into medicines and materials.

name: Percy Liang
blurb: Percy Liang directs Stanford's Center for Research on Foundation Models — the group that coined the term 'foundation model' — and created HELM, the standard for rigorous model evaluation. He is a leading advocate for open, transparent AI development.

name: Kaiming He
blurb: Kaiming He invented ResNet, the residual-network architecture that is among the most-cited works in modern science and made very deep neural networks trainable. Now at MIT after years at Meta AI, his innovations (Mask R-CNN, MAE) run inside virtually every vision system.

name: Liang Wenfeng
blurb: Liang Wenfeng founded DeepSeek, whose R1 reasoning model stunned the world in January 2025 by matching frontier performance at a fraction of the training cost — wiping hundreds of billions off US tech valuations in a day. Funded by his quant fund High-Flyer, DeepSeek made China a first-tier force in open frontier models.

name: Yang Zhilin
blurb: Yang Zhilin, a Tsinghua- and CMU-trained researcher behind Transformer-XL and XLNet, founded Moonshot AI, one of China's 'AI tiger' startups. Its Kimi assistant pioneered ultra-long-context chat and its open K2 models rank among the strongest agentic models globally.

name: Zhang Peng
blurb: Zhang Peng leads Zhipu AI, the Tsinghua-born lab behind the GLM model family and one of the first Chinese AI companies to pursue a public listing. Zhipu's open GLM releases and enterprise platform made it a national champion for China's foundation-model industry.

name: Tang Jie
blurb: Tang Jie, a Tsinghua professor, led the research that produced the GLM family of large models and co-founded Zhipu AI's technical program. He is one of China's most-cited AI researchers, bridging academic scale-model research and commercial deployment.

name: Yan Junjie
blurb: Yan Junjie founded MiniMax, the Shanghai lab behind the Hailuo video-generation models, the ABAB/MiniMax LLM series, and hit consumer AI companion apps used worldwide. MiniMax's efficient linear-attention architectures and 2025 Hong Kong IPO made it a bellwether for China's AI startups.

name: Jiang Daxin
blurb: Jiang Daxin, formerly a Microsoft engineering VP who led NLP research in Asia, founded StepFun, an 'AI tiger' known for its Step series of multimodal foundation models. StepFun is a leading Chinese contender in vision-language and audio frontier models.

name: Wang Xiaochuan
blurb: Wang Xiaochuan, founder of search engine Sogou, launched Baichuan AI, whose open Baichuan models were among China's earliest credible LLMs and now focus on AI for healthcare. He is one of the most prominent second-time founders in China's model race.

name: Kai-Fu Lee
blurb: Kai-Fu Lee — former head of Google China and author of 'AI Superpowers' — founded 01.AI, whose Yi models topped open-source leaderboards, and has funded a generation of Chinese AI startups through Sinovation Ventures. He remains the most recognizable bridge figure between the US and Chinese AI ecosystems.

name: Li Dahai
blurb: Li Dahai, former Zhihu CTO, leads ModelBest, whose MiniCPM 'little cannon' models deliver frontier-class capability at sizes small enough to run on phones and in cars. ModelBest is China's standard-bearer for efficient edge AI.

name: Liu Zhiyuan
blurb: Liu Zhiyuan, a Tsinghua NLP professor, co-founded ModelBest and drives the research behind the MiniCPM efficient model family. His group's work on knowledge-infused and small-footprint LLMs shapes how AI reaches consumer devices.

name: Robin Li
blurb: Robin Li built Baidu, China's dominant search engine, and moved earliest among Chinese giants into AI — launching Ernie Bot, the Apollo autonomous-driving platform, and the Kunlun AI chip line. Baidu's Apollo Go operates one of the world's largest robotaxi fleets.

name: Wang Haifeng
blurb: Wang Haifeng, Baidu's CTO and the first Chinese president of the ACL, leads the engineering behind the Ernie foundation models and Baidu's PaddlePaddle deep-learning framework — China's most widely used homegrown AI platform.

name: Shen Dou
blurb: Shen Dou runs Baidu AI Cloud, the business arm that commercializes Ernie models for Chinese enterprises and government, making Baidu one of the largest providers of AI cloud services in China.

name: Eddie Wu (Wu Yongming)
blurb: Eddie Wu refocused Alibaba around an 'AI-first' strategy, committing over $50 billion to AI and cloud infrastructure and elevating the Qwen open-model family into the world's most-downloaded open-weight model line. Under him Alibaba became the clearest Chinese counterpart to the US hyperscalers' AI push.

name: Joe Tsai
blurb: Joe Tsai, Alibaba's co-founder and chairman, has been the public architect of its AI reinvention — championing massive AI capex and open-sourcing the Qwen models. He is among the most influential voices connecting Chinese AI to global capital markets.

name: Zhou Jingren
blurb: Zhou Jingren leads the research and engineering behind Alibaba's Qwen (Tongyi Qianwen) models, whose open releases across every size and modality made them the foundation for thousands of derivative models worldwide.

name: Lin Junyang
blurb: Lin Junyang is the technical lead of Alibaba's Qwen team, driving the model line that consistently tops open-weight leaderboards and powers a global ecosystem of fine-tuned models — arguably open-source AI's most influential engineering effort.

name: Wang Jian
blurb: Wang Jian founded Alibaba Cloud — China's largest cloud — and championed the 'city brain' concept of AI-managed urban infrastructure. A Chinese Academy of Engineering academician, he now drives national research programs in intelligent computing.

name: Pony Ma
blurb: Pony Ma leads Tencent, whose Hunyuan foundation models, open-source 3D and video models, and AI integration across WeChat's billion-plus users make it one of the world's most consequential AI deployers. Tencent's Yuanbao assistant became one of China's most-used AI apps.

name: Zhang Zhengyou
blurb: Zhang Zhengyou, inventor of the camera-calibration method used in virtually every computer-vision pipeline ('Zhang's method'), is Tencent's Chief Scientist and leads its Robotics X lab building embodied AI.

name: Zhang Yiming
blurb: Zhang Yiming founded ByteDance, whose recommendation algorithms redefined global media through TikTok/Douyin — the most commercially successful applied-AI system ever built. ByteDance's Doubao models and Seed research group now anchor one of the world's largest AI investments.

name: Liang Rubo
blurb: Liang Rubo, ByteDance's co-founder and CEO, directs one of the largest AI capital programs on earth — the Doubao model family, video-generation systems like Seedance, and AI features across apps used by billions.

name: Wu Yonghui
blurb: Wu Yonghui, a former Google Fellow who helped lead Google's translation and Gemini efforts, now heads foundation-model research at ByteDance Seed — one of the most significant US-to-China talent moves in frontier AI.

name: Ren Zhengfei
blurb: Ren Zhengfei steered Huawei through US sanctions to build a full domestic AI stack — Ascend AI chips, the MindSpore framework, and Pangu industry models — making Huawei the hardware backbone of China's AI self-sufficiency drive.

name: Eric Xu (Xu Zhijun)
blurb: Eric Xu oversees Huawei's AI strategy, including the Ascend chip roadmap and CloudMatrix AI clusters that have become China's leading alternative to NVIDIA systems. He has been the chief public architect of Huawei's 'AI for industries' push.

name: Lei Jun
blurb: Lei Jun leads Xiaomi's expansion from smartphones into AI-defined EVs (the hit SU7), on-device MiMo models, and a vast AIoT ecosystem — a bet that AI's biggest business is intelligent hardware at consumer scale.

name: Luo Fuli
blurb: Luo Fuli, a key young researcher on DeepSeek's V2 models dubbed an 'AI prodigy' in Chinese media, was recruited by Lei Jun to help lead Xiaomi's large-model effort — emblematic of the fierce talent race inside China's AI industry.

name: Zhou Hongyi
blurb: Zhou Hongyi drives 360 Group's pivot from cybersecurity to 'security + AI', shipping the Nano AI agent products and free enterprise security models — and is one of China's most vocal evangelists for AI agents.

name: Su Hua
blurb: Su Hua co-founded Kuaishou, whose Kling video-generation model leapt to the global frontier of AI video and turned the short-video giant into a serious foundation-model player with real revenue from generative tools.

name: Liu Qingfeng
blurb: Liu Qingfeng built iFlytek into China's speech-AI champion; its Spark models and translation devices are deployed across education, healthcare, and government. iFlytek trains its models entirely on Huawei's domestic Ascend chips — a milestone for China's independent AI stack.

name: Wang Xingxing
blurb: Wang Xingxing founded Unitree, whose affordable, backflipping humanoids and robot dogs became the global face of China's robotics surge — from the Spring Festival Gala stage to research labs worldwide. Unitree made advanced legged robots a mass-producible product.

name: Peng Zhihui
blurb: Peng Zhihui — the star engineer known online as 'Zhihui Jun' — co-founded AgiBot, which mass-produces general-purpose humanoids and released some of the largest open embodied-AI datasets. He personifies China's maker-to-industrialist robotics pipeline.

name: Wang He
blurb: Wang He, a Peking University professor, founded Galbot, whose wheeled humanoids run unmanned retail stores and pioneered sim-to-real generalizable grasping. Galbot is a leading example of embodied foundation models reaching commercial deployment.

name: He Xiaopeng
blurb: He Xiaopeng leads XPeng's transformation into an 'AI automaker' — its end-to-end autonomous-driving stack, in-house Turing AI chips, Iron humanoid robot, and flying-car subsidiary map one of the broadest physical-AI portfolios anywhere.

name: Li Xiang
blurb: Li Xiang built Li Auto into one of China's top EV makers and pushed it aggressively into AI with the MindVLA driving model and Li Xiang Tongxue assistant — treating the car as an embodied AI agent for families.

name: William Li (Li Bin)
blurb: William Li founded NIO, pioneering battery-swap EVs and shipping the in-house Shenji NX9031 autonomous-driving chip — one of the first 5nm automotive AI processors designed by a carmaker anywhere.

name: James Peng
blurb: James Peng co-founded Pony.ai, which operates fully driverless robotaxi fleets in multiple Chinese megacities and listed on Nasdaq in 2024 — one of the first pure-play autonomous-driving companies to reach public markets.

name: Tony Han
blurb: Tony Han founded WeRide, the first robotaxi company listed on Nasdaq and the first to hold driverless permits in China, the UAE, Singapore, and the US — making it the most internationally deployed autonomous-driving operator.

name: Yu Kai
blurb: Yu Kai, who founded Baidu's deep-learning institute before starting Horizon Robotics, built China's leading automotive AI-chip company — its Journey processors power smart driving in millions of vehicles from dozens of automakers.

name: Fu Sheng
blurb: Fu Sheng pivoted Cheetah Mobile into service robotics through OrionStar, whose reception, delivery, and coffee robots are deployed across thousands of hotels, hospitals, and restaurants in dozens of countries.

name: Chen Tianshi
blurb: Chen Tianshi, a former Chinese Academy of Sciences prodigy, founded Cambricon, China's flagship listed AI-chip designer. Its accelerators became a core domestic alternative for AI training as export controls reshaped the market, briefly making Cambricon China's most valuable stock by price.

name: Zhou Bowen
blurb: Zhou Bowen, former JD.com AI head and IBM researcher, directs the Shanghai AI Laboratory — China's premier state AI lab — overseeing the InternLM open models and national research on safe, scientific AI.

name: Harry Shum (Shen Xiangyang)
blurb: Harry Shum, who ran Microsoft's worldwide AI and Research group as EVP, now chairs the IDEA Research institute in Shenzhen, incubating open vision models and AI startups — one of the deepest research bridges between the two AI superpowers.

name: Zhang Yaqin
role: Dean, Institute for AI Industry Research
blurb: Zhang Yaqin, former Baidu president and Microsoft corporate VP, founded and leads Tsinghua's Institute for AI Industry Research (AIR), training China's next generation of AI leaders and steering research in autonomous driving and AI for science.

name: Andrew Chi-Chih Yao
blurb: Andrew Yao, the only Chinese Turing Award laureate, built Tsinghua's elite 'Yao Class', whose alumni founded many of China's top AI companies (including Megvii and Pony.ai). He remains the intellectual godfather of China's AI talent pipeline.

name: Xu Li
blurb: Xu Li co-founded SenseTime, once the world's most valuable AI startup, and led its pivot from computer vision to the SenseNova foundation-model platform and large-scale AI data centers across China.

name: Yin Qi
blurb: Yin Qi co-founded Megvii (Face++), one of the companies that made China a computer-vision superpower, and has steered it toward AIoT and, more recently, intelligent-driving systems.

name: Yan Shuicheng
blurb: Yan Shuicheng, one of the world's most-cited AI researchers, is chief scientist behind Kunlun Tech's Skywork models — a prolific open-source line spanning reasoning, agents, and AI music that punches far above the company's size.

name: Dai Wenyuan
blurb: Dai Wenyuan, a champion competitive programmer and transfer-learning researcher, founded 4Paradigm, the Hong Kong-listed enterprise-AI platform that brings decision-making AI to banks, retailers, and manufacturers across China.

name: Qi Lu
blurb: Qi Lu — former Microsoft EVP and Baidu COO who launched Baidu's Apollo self-driving platform — runs MiraclePlus (Y Combinator China's successor), the accelerator seeding hundreds of Chinese AI and hard-tech startups.
